items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 90:1
items.html: Malchut is called a corner, because Malchut is the last of the ten Sefirot, like the corner of the field left at the end of the harvest. Hence the Malchut of the ten Sefirot of the hairs of the head is called the corners of the head. And this Malchut of the corners of the head is like the membrane of the Avir that separates between the Galgalta, which is the MEM of Tzelem, and the Avir and the Sealed Brain, which are the LAMED-TZADIK of Tzelem. For likewise the Malchut of the hairs of the head separates between the hairs of the head, which are the aspect of the MEM of Tzelem, and the hairs of the beard, which are the aspect of the LAMED-TZADIK of Tzelem. Hence the hairs of the beard come out from the corners of the head. And it is also discerned that there is in it from the aspect of the Malchut of the first restriction, for the aspect of the hairs is the garments of the revealed AB, which comes out upon the aspect of the Malchut of the first restriction, as is known. (Page 382, Item 178).
